frequency_question: How often do structural institutional friction points (such as divergent regulatory standards, labor/environmental chapters, and domestic veto actors) successfully block the formal signing of major bilateral trade agreements within a defined timeline?
membership_rule: Includes all comprehensive bilateral trade agreements negotiated between the EU and major non-EU G20 economies initiated or advanced since 2004 that encountered substantive structural friction. Excluded are minor technical cooperation pacts or investment-only treaties lacking comprehensive trade scope.

cases.name: EU-India Bilateral Trade and Investment Agreement (Initial talks paused/resumed)
EU-Mercosur Trade Agreement (Finalised text awaiting signature/ratification)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
EU-Australia Free Trade Agreement (Stalled over agricultural quotas)

coverage_note: 8 major modern EU comprehensive trade negotiation efforts examined; represents the core population of comparable scale.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller preferential trade arrangements with developing regions that lacked complex structural friction points.
skeleton: Major bilateral trade agreement negotiation cycles involving the EU and major partners where structural friction is actively tested against a closing window.
multiplier: 5 hits / 3 misses out of 8 total recorded comprehensive trade negotiation cycles subject to deep structural friction.
validity_reason: Trade negotiation architectures and EU institutional veto dynamics remain stable over medium-term political cycles, but evolve as new sustainability and border adjustment mechanisms are introduced.
